components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 捆 is tying up a bundle.
困 (kùn) — close sound: 捆 kǔn. 困 also sounds out 睏 kùn.

example.hanzi: 他把书捆成一捆。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shū kǔn chéng yì kǔn.
example.english: He tied the books into a bundle.
example.fact: 捆 is both a verb and a measure word: 一捆柴 (a bundle of firewood). 捆绑销售 means bundled sales.

examples.hanzi: 他把柴火捆成一捆一捆的。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ cháihuo kǔn chéng yì kǔn yì kǔn de.
examples.english: He tied the firewood into bundles.

examples.hanzi: 请用绳子把箱子捆紧。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng shéngzi bǎ xiāngzi kǔn jǐn.
examples.english: Please tie the box tightly with rope.

components.note: 凯 (kǎi) — triumph, mostly seen in names; as a part it sounds out 铠 kǎi and 恺 kǎi.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 凯利来自澳大利亚,现在在北京工作。
example.pinyin: Kǎilì láizì Àodàlìyà, xiànzài zài Běijīng gōngzuò.
example.english: Kelly is from Australia and now works in Beijing.
example.fact: Australia's platypus, one of only five living monotreme species, was first described by European naturalists in 1799 — who initially suspected the specimen was a hoax, an animal stitched together from parts of a duck and a mammal, since no such creature was known to lay eggs while also producing milk.

examples.hanzi: 凯利喜欢在周末烤蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Kǎilì xǐhuan zài zhōumò kǎo dàngāo.
examples.english: Kelly likes baking cakes on weekends.

examples.hanzi: 我今天在超市遇到了凯利。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān zài chāoshì yùdào le Kǎilì.
examples.english: I ran into Kelly at the supermarket today.

components.note: 冏 (bright/window) — the lower part; dictionary treats it as the 'bright' hint. Meaning 'trade, business' is better remembered as a market (商店).
口 (mouth) — dictionary radical, as in 吃 eat. Memory aid: a shop-keeper's mouth calling out prices; 商量 is to 'talk it over'.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 这家商店卖各种各样的商品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn mài gèzhǒng gèyàng de shāngpǐn.
example.english: This store sells all kinds of merchandise.
example.fact: The Dutch tulip mania of 1637 is often cited as the world's first recorded speculative economic bubble: at its peak, single rare tulip bulbs traded for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled craftsman, before prices collapsed within weeks.

examples.hanzi: 这些商品都打了八折。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shāngpǐn dōu dǎ le bā zhé.
examples.english: All these goods are 20 percent off.

examples.hanzi: 网上商品的种类比商店里多。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngshàng shāngpǐn de zhǒnglèi bǐ shāngdiàn lǐ duō.
examples.english: There are more kinds of goods online than in stores.

meanings: variant of 反覆|反复[fan3 fu4]

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.
复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.

example.hanzi: 他反复练习这首曲子,直到弹得完美。
example.pinyin: Tā fǎnfù liànxí zhè shǒu qǔzi, zhídào tán de wánměi.
example.english: He practiced this piece of music repeatedly until he could play it perfectly.
example.fact: In 1885, German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus published the 'forgetting curve,' showing that newly learned information fades rapidly within days unless it is deliberately reviewed — a finding that still underlies modern spaced-repetition study techniques.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题他反复问了好几遍。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí tā fǎnfù wèn le hǎo jǐ biàn.
examples.english: He asked this question again and again.

examples.hanzi: 病情反复，医生让他继续住院。
examples.pinyin: Bìngqíng fǎnfù, yīshēng ràng tā jìxù zhùyuàn.
examples.english: His condition kept relapsing, so the doctor had him stay in the hospital.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and flowing things, as in 河, 海, 汤; 波 is a wave.
皮 (pí) is a loose hint for bō; 坡 pō and 破 pò share it.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 工程师用波特率来衡量数据传输的速度。
example.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī yòng bōtèlǜ lái héngliáng shùjù chuánshū de sùdù.
example.english: Engineers use baud rate to measure the speed of data transmission.
example.fact: The baud, a unit measuring signal changes per second in telecommunications, is named after Émile Baudot, a French engineer who invented an early digital telegraph code in the 1870s that let multiple messages share a single telegraph line.

examples.hanzi: 老师给我们讲了波特先生的故事。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen jiǎng le Bōtè xiānsheng de gùshi.
examples.english: The teacher told us the story of Mr. Potter.

examples.hanzi: 波特是我们球队新来的教练。
examples.pinyin: Bōtè shì wǒmen qiúduì xīn lái de jiàoliàn.
examples.english: Porter is the new coach of our team.

meanings: to get hit by a bullet

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
弓 (bow) — bows and tension: 张 stretch, 引 draw, 弯 bend; 弹 is to shoot or spring, and a bullet.
单 (dān) is a loose clue for dàn/tán; compare 禅 chán and 蝉 chán.

example.hanzi: 那名士兵在战斗中中弹受伤。
example.pinyin: Nà míng shìbīng zài zhàndòu zhōng zhòngdàn shòushāng.
example.english: That soldier was hit by a bullet and wounded in the battle.
example.fact: A bullet fired from an AK-47 travels at roughly 715 meters per second, more than twice the speed of sound. That is why a supersonic bullet passing overhead produces a sharp crack that reaches an observer's ear before the sound of the gunshot itself.

examples.hanzi: 他的腿中弹了，被送去医院抢救。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ zhòngdàn le, bèi sòng qù yīyuàn qiǎngjiù.
examples.english: He was shot in the leg and rushed to the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的英雄中弹后依然继续前进。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de yīngxióng zhòngdàn hòu yīrán jìxù qiánjìn.
examples.english: The hero in the movie kept moving forward even after being shot.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.

example.hanzi: 她大学时主修生化专业。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué shí zhǔxiū shēnghuà zhuānyè.
example.english: She majored in biochemistry in college.
example.fact: The double-helix structure of DNA, announced by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953, relied heavily on X-ray diffraction images produced by chemist Rosalind Franklin, whose crucial contribution went largely unrecognized during her lifetime.

examples.hanzi: 他研究生化，每天都在实验室里。
examples.pinyin: Tā yánjiū shēnghuà, měi tiān dōu zài shíyànshì lǐ.
examples.english: He studies biochemistry and is in the lab every day.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的生化危机把整个城市变成了废墟。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de shēnghuà wēijī bǎ zhěnggè chéngshì biànchéng le fèixū.
examples.english: The biochemical crisis in the movie turned the whole city into ruins.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their relationships, as in 你, 信 trust, 借 borrow; a debt is what a person owes.
责 (zé) — loose sound hint (zhài vs zé), but 责 also means duty, which fits owing a debt; same part in 积 jī.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.

example.hanzi: 这个国家背负着巨额债务。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā bèifù zhe jù'é zhàiwù.
example.english: This country is carrying a huge amount of debt.
example.fact: The earliest known written debt records are Mesopotamian clay tablets dating back roughly 5,000 years, which recorded loans of grain, silver, and livestock between merchants — making debt one of the oldest documented human institutions.

examples.hanzi: 他每个月都要还债务，压力很大。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi gè yuè dōu yào huán zhàiwù, yālì hěn dà.
examples.english: He has to repay his debts every month and is under great pressure.

examples.hanzi: 公司的债务问题越来越严重。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī de zhàiwù wèntí yuèláiyuè yánzhòng.
examples.english: The company's debt problem is getting worse.

components.note: 人 (person) — the roof-like top. 余 absorbed 餘 (food left over); the shape no longer explains 'remainder'. Memory aid: a person with leftovers.
食 (food) — the old 餘 had the food part 饣; 余 is its sound part (yú), the same series as 除 chú, 徐 xú, 途 tú, with loose matches.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 这个计划安排得很紧,没有留下失败的余地。
example.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà ānpái de hěn jǐn, méiyǒu liú xià shībài de yúdì.
example.english: This plan is scheduled so tightly that it leaves no room for failure.
example.fact: The Brooklyn Bridge, completed in 1883, was built with roughly six times the strength its engineers calculated it would ever need — a wide safety margin that chief engineer Washington Roebling insisted on after discovering a supplier had sold the project substandard cable wire.

examples.hanzi: 这件事还有商量的余地吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hái yǒu shāngliang de yúdì ma?
examples.english: Is there still room for discussion on this matter?

examples.hanzi: 房间太小，连放张桌子的余地都没有。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān tài xiǎo, lián fàng zhāng zhuōzi de yúdì dōu méiyǒu.
examples.english: The room is so small that there is no room even for a table.

meanings: to be later than the time stipulated or agreed upon

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 这种手机型号已经过时了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shǒujī xínghào yǐjīng guòshí le.
example.english: This model of phone is already out of date.
example.fact: The original iPhone, released in 2007, shipped with just 128 megabytes of RAM — less memory than many basic smartwatches carry today, a reminder of how quickly computing hardware becomes obsolete.

examples.hanzi: 你这件衣服的款式有点过时了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè jiàn yīfu de kuǎnshì yǒudiǎn guòshí le.
examples.english: The style of this garment is a bit outdated.

examples.hanzi: 他的想法已经过时，跟不上时代了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiǎngfǎ yǐjīng guòshí, gēn bu shàng shídài le.
examples.english: His ideas are out of date and can't keep up with the times.

components.note: 片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).
殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand with a tool striking, as in 毁, 殴; 段 is a piece cut off a larger whole, and sounds out 锻 duàn.

example.hanzi: 我只记得那部电影的几个片段。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ jìde nà bù diànyǐng de jǐ gè piànduàn.
example.english: I only remember a few fragments of that movie.
example.fact: Almost all of the ancient Greek poet Sappho's work survives only in fragments, preserved mostly on scraps of papyrus recovered from Egyptian rubbish heaps; new fragments of her poetry are still occasionally discovered, including a significant find published in 2014.

examples.hanzi: 我只看了这个电影的片段。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ kàn le zhège diànyǐng de piànduàn.
examples.english: I only watched fragments of this movie.

examples.hanzi: 他把童年的片段写进了书里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóngnián de piànduàn xiě jìn le shū lǐ.
examples.english: He wrote snippets of his childhood into the book.

meanings: erhua variant of 大伙[da4 huo3]

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 大伙儿一起去爬山吧。
example.pinyin: Dàhuǒr yīqǐ qù páshān ba.
example.english: Let's all go hiking together.
example.fact: Emperor penguins survive Antarctic winters by huddling together in groups of thousands, and individuals continually rotate position so that everyone takes a turn standing in the warmer center of the huddle rather than the colder outer edge.

examples.hanzi: 大伙儿今天晚上去哪儿吃饭？
examples.pinyin: Dàhuǒr jīntiān wǎnshang qù nǎr chīfàn?
examples.english: Where are we all going to eat tonight?

examples.hanzi: 大伙儿都很喜欢新来的同事。
examples.pinyin: Dàhuǒr dōu hěn xǐhuan xīn lái de tóngshì.
examples.english: Everyone likes the new colleague.

components.note: 氵 (water) — slippery as wet surfaces; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
骨 (gǔ) is only a loose sound clue; 猾 huá shares it and sounds exactly like 滑.
木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 桌, 桥; 板 is a plank or board.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match (-an); same part in 饭 fàn and 版 bǎn.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在公园里玩滑板。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài gōngyuán lǐ wán huábǎn.
example.english: He likes skateboarding in the park.
example.fact: Skateboards were invented by California surfers in the 1950s who wanted a way to practice their sport on land. The sport was transformed in the early 1970s when Frank Nasworthy introduced polyurethane wheels, which gripped the pavement far better than the clay wheels used before.

examples.hanzi: 他的滑板是爸爸送的生日礼物。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huábǎn shì bàba sòng de shēngrì lǐwù.
examples.english: His skateboard was a birthday gift from his dad.

examples.hanzi: 这个男孩滑板玩得特别好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège nánhái huábǎn wán de tèbié hǎo.
examples.english: This boy is especially good at skateboarding.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 本案将由三名法官共同审理。
example.pinyin: Běn'àn jiāng yóu sān míng fǎguān gòngtóng shěnlǐ.
example.english: This case will be jointly tried by three judges.
example.fact: The Nuremberg trials of 1945–46 established a lasting precedent for prosecuting crimes against humanity, with judges from four different Allied nations — the US, UK, France, and the Soviet Union — sitting together on the same bench to hear evidence.

examples.hanzi: 本案的关键证人是一位老人。
examples.pinyin: Běn'àn de guānjiàn zhèngrén shì yí wèi lǎorén.
examples.english: The key witness in this case is an old man.

examples.hanzi: 法官宣布本案将择日再审。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān xuānbù běn'àn jiāng zérì zàishěn.
examples.english: The judge announced that this case will be retried at a later date.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 衤 is the clothing radical, as in 衣, 裤, 衬; 被 is a quilt, then the passive marker.
皮 (pí) — loose hint — 被 is bèi; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī and 坡 pō.
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.

example.hanzi: 被害人是一名年轻女子。
example.pinyin: Bèihàirén shì yī míng niánqīng nǚzǐ.
example.english: The victim was a young woman.
example.fact: Forensic entomologists can estimate how long a body has been deceased by studying blowfly activity: blowflies typically lay eggs on remains within minutes of death, and the developmental stage of the resulting larvae provides a reliable biological clock.

examples.hanzi: 被害人家属希望法院严惩凶手。
examples.pinyin: Bèihàirén jiāshǔ xīwàng fǎyuàn yánchéng xiōngshǒu.
examples.english: The victim's family hopes the court will punish the culprit severely.

examples.hanzi: 这起事件中，被害人没有受伤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ shìjiàn zhōng, bèihàirén méiyǒu shòushāng.
examples.english: In this incident, the victim was not injured.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.

example.hanzi: 专家预计明年经济会有所增长。
example.pinyin: Zhuānjiā yùjì míngnián jīngjì huì yǒu suǒ zēngzhǎng.
example.english: Experts forecast that the economy will grow somewhat next year.
example.fact: Weather forecasting accuracy has improved so dramatically that a modern five-day forecast is now about as reliable as a one-day forecast was in the 1980s, thanks to satellite data, ocean buoys, and vastly greater computing power.

examples.hanzi: 预计明天会有大雨。
examples.pinyin: Yùjì míngtiān huì yǒu dàyǔ.
examples.english: Heavy rain is expected tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这个项目预计三个月完成。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù yùjì sān gè yuè wánchéng.
examples.english: This project is expected to be finished in three months.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 媒 is a matchmaker, as in 媒体 media.
某 (mǒu) — near sound — 媒 is méi; 某 also sounds out 煤 méi and 谋 móu.

example.hanzi: 现在人们通过社交媒体联系。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài rénmen tōngguò shèjiāo méitǐ liánxì.
example.english: Nowadays people stay in touch through social media.
example.fact: 媒 originally meant matchmaker (媒人). It later extended to 'medium': 媒体 (media), 传媒, 媒介.

examples.hanzi: 她在一家媒体公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā méitǐ gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: She works at a media company.

examples.hanzi: 这条新闻已经被各大媒体报道了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīnwén yǐjīng bèi gè dà méitǐ bàodào le.
examples.english: This news has been reported by major media outlets.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 撬 is prying open with a lever.

example.hanzi: 小偷撬开了窗户。
example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qiào kāi le chuānghu.
example.english: The thief pried the window open.
example.fact: 撬 gives 撬锁 (pick a lock), 撬棍 (crowbar) and 撬墙脚 (to poach a partner or employee).

examples.hanzi: 他用铁棍把盖子撬开了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng tiěgùn bǎ gàizi qiào kāi le.
examples.english: He pried the lid open with an iron bar.

examples.hanzi: 小偷想撬锁进屋。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu xiǎng qiào suǒ jìn wū.
examples.english: The thief wanted to pick the lock and get in.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — striking or acting: 教, 放, 政; 敌 is an opponent to strike.
舌 here is a form of 啇 (dí), the sound part; also in 滴 dī and 嫡 dí.

example.hanzi: 我们不能轻敌。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng qīngdí.
example.english: We can't underestimate the enemy.
example.fact: 敌 gives 敌人 (enemy), 敌意 (hostility), 无敌 (invincible), 轻敌 (underestimate) and 情敌 (love rival).

examples.hanzi: 大家都把他看作敌人。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu bǎ tā kànzuò dírén.
examples.english: Everyone regards him as an enemy.

examples.hanzi: 这支球队的实力无人能敌。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì de shílì wú rén néng dí.
examples.english: This team's strength has no match.

components.note: 风 (wind; traditional 風) — marks wind and air, as in 飘 drift, 飓 hurricane; 飙 is a whirlwind, as in 飙车 speed.
猋 (biāo) — three dogs 犬 racing: a running storm; same part in 飙 biāo.

example.hanzi: 他开车飙到了一百八。
example.pinyin: Tā kāichē biāo dào le yì bǎi bā.
example.english: He drove up to 180.
example.fact: 飙 is slang: 飙车 (street racing), 飙升 (skyrocket), 飙泪 (burst into tears). Originally it meant a violent wind.

examples.hanzi: 他的车子飙得太快了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chēzi biāo de tài kuài le.
examples.english: His car was speeding too fast.

examples.hanzi: 最近天气很热，气温一路飙升。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn tiānqì hěn rè, qìwēn yílù biāoshēng.
examples.english: The weather is hot lately and temperatures keep soaring.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 逃; 避 is stepping aside.
辟 (bì) — same sound — 避 is bì, like 辟; 辟 also sounds out 壁 bì and 臂 bì.

example.hanzi: 我们找了个地方避雨。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǎo le gè dìfang bì yǔ.
example.english: We found a place to shelter from the rain.
example.fact: 避 gives 避免 (avoid), 避开 (steer clear of), 逃避 (escape), 避孕 (contraception), 避暑 (escape the heat).

examples.hanzi: 外面下雨了，我们先避一避。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn xià yǔ le, wǒmen xiān bì yi bì.
examples.english: It is raining outside, so let's take shelter first.

examples.hanzi: 这样做可以避免很多麻烦。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò kěyǐ bìmiǎn hěn duō máfan.
examples.english: Doing this can avoid a lot of trouble.

components.note: 刂 (knife; 刀) — marks cutting, as in 刻 carve, 划 draw, 别 separate; 删 is cutting something out.
册 (cè, bound booklet) — cutting writing out of a book: delete, as in 删除.

example.hanzi: 我把那条消息删了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ nà tiáo xiāoxi shān le.
example.english: I deleted that message.
example.fact: 删 is the everyday verb for deleting files and messages: 删除 (delete), 删掉, 删减 (cut down). Its original sense was trimming bamboo-slip books with a knife.

examples.hanzi: 你可以把没用的照片删掉。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bǎ méi yòng de zhàopiàn shān diào.
examples.english: You can delete the useless photos.

examples.hanzi: 请不要随意删改这份文件。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng búyào suíyì shāngǎi zhè fèn wénjiàn.
examples.english: Please do not delete or edit this file at will.

components.note: 书 (simplified 書) — the old form shows a brush 聿 writing; to write, then what is written: book, letter.
广 (building, shelter) — houses and shops: 床, 库, 座; 店 is a shop.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound hint; same part in 站 zhàn and 战 zhàn.

example.hanzi: 巷子拐角有一家小书店。
example.pinyin: Xiàngzi guǎijiǎo yǒu yī jiā xiǎo shūdiàn.
example.english: There is a small bookstore at the corner of the alley.
example.fact: Shakespeare and Company, an English-language bookstore founded in Paris in 1919, became a gathering place for expatriate writers such as Ernest Hemingway and F. Scott Fitzgerald, who sometimes borrowed money or slept there when they were broke.

examples.hanzi: 我周末常去书店看书。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò cháng qù shūdiàn kàn shū.
examples.english: I often go to the bookstore to read on weekends.

examples.hanzi: 学校旁边新开了一家书店。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào pángbiān xīn kāi le yì jiā shūdiàn.
examples.english: A new bookstore opened next to the school.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 同事们午休时说笑聊天,气氛很轻松。
example.pinyin: Tóngshìmen wǔxiū shí shuōxiào liáotiān, qìfēn hěn qīngsōng.
example.english: Colleagues chat and joke during their lunch break, keeping the mood relaxed.
example.fact: Laughter is highly contagious: studies of social behavior find people are roughly thirty times more likely to laugh when they are with others than when they are alone, which is one reason sitcoms use a laugh track.

examples.hanzi: 朋友们一边吃饭一边说笑。
examples.pinyin: Péngyoumen yìbiān chīfàn yìbiān shuōxiào.
examples.english: Friends chat and laugh as they eat.

examples.hanzi: 她爱说笑，大家都喜欢和她聊天。
examples.pinyin: Tā ài shuōxiào, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan hé tā liáotiān.
examples.english: She loves to joke around, and everyone likes chatting with her.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 私 was grain held for oneself.
厶 (sī) is the ancient form of 私 itself, meaning private; 公 gōng (public) is its opposite.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 这是我的私事,请不要过问。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de sīshì, qǐng bùyào guòwèn.
example.english: This is my personal matter, please don't ask about it.
example.fact: The modern legal concept of a 'right to privacy' traces largely to an 1890 Harvard Law Review article by Samuel Warren and Louis Brandeis, written partly in response to intrusive newspaper photography made possible by the newly portable handheld camera.

examples.hanzi: 这是私事，我想自己处理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì sīshì, wǒ xiǎng zìjǐ chǔlǐ.
examples.english: This is a personal matter, and I want to handle it myself.

examples.hanzi: 上班时间不要处理私事。
examples.pinyin: Shàngbān shíjiān búyào chǔlǐ sīshì.
examples.english: Don't deal with personal matters during work hours.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 汤 soup; a hole as eroded by flowing water.
同 (tóng) — sound hint is loose (dòng vs tóng); 同 also sounds out 铜 tóng and 筒 tǒng.
穴 (cave) — roof 宀 over 八 (digging), a dug-out den. As radical 穴 appears in 空 empty, 窗 window, 穷 poor, all about hollows.

example.hanzi: 考古学家在洞穴里发现了古代壁画。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài dòngxué lǐ fāxiàn le gǔdài bìhuà.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered ancient cave paintings inside the cave.
example.fact: The Lascaux cave in southwestern France, discovered in 1940 by four teenagers chasing their dog into a hole in the ground, contains paintings of horses, bulls, and deer estimated to be around 17,000 years old.

examples.hanzi: 蝙蝠白天躲在洞穴里睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Biānfú báitiān duǒ zài dòngxué lǐ shuìjiào.
examples.english: Bats sleep in caves during the day.

examples.hanzi: 他们带着手电筒进了洞穴。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dàizhe shǒudiàntǒng jìn le dòngxué.
examples.english: They entered the cave with flashlights.

meanings: to go on an official or business trip

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
羊 (sheep) — the sheep family: 美, 养, 群. Dictionary story: work 工 done by a sheep — memory aid for being poor or off. Origin uncertain.
工 (work) — the bottom. Memory aid: poor work 工, so 差劲 poor quality. 差 is chā/chà (difference, lacking) or chāi (send).

example.hanzi: 他下周要去上海出差。
example.pinyin: Tā xià zhōu yào qù Shànghǎi chūchāi.
example.english: He is going on a business trip to Shanghai next week.
example.fact: A traveler's circadian clock generally needs about one full day to adjust for every time zone crossed, which is why crossing several zones on a business trip often produces jet lag that lingers for nearly a week.

examples.hanzi: 经理下个月要去北京出差。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ xià gè yuè yào qù Běijīng chūchāi.
examples.english: The manager is going to Beijing on a business trip next month.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸经常出差，不常在家。
examples.pinyin: Bàba jīngcháng chūchāi, bù cháng zài jiā.
examples.english: Dad often travels for work and isn't home much.

meanings: to carry on a clandestine love affair

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 住; 偷 is a person stealing.
俞 (yú) is a loose hint for tōu; 愉 yú and 输 shū share it.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 这部小说描写了一段偷情的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō miáoxiě le yī duàn tōuqíng de gùshì.
example.english: This novel depicts a story of a clandestine love affair.
example.fact: Leo Tolstoy's 1877 novel Anna Karenina, built around its heroine's affair, opens with one of the most quoted lines in world literature — 'All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way' — a line Tolstoy is said to have revised many times before publication.

examples.hanzi: 这部电视剧讲的是一个偷情引发的家庭矛盾。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànshìjù jiǎng de shì yí gè tōuqíng yǐnfā de jiātíng máodùn.
examples.english: This TV drama is about a family conflict triggered by an affair.

examples.hanzi: 有人说他和同事偷情，但没有证据。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén shuō tā hé tóngshì tōuqíng, dàn méiyǒu zhèngjù.
examples.english: Someone said he was having an affair with a colleague, but there is no proof.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 阿 first meant a slope.
可 (kě) — near sound — 阿 is ā; 可 also sounds out 河 hé and 哥 gē.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.

example.hanzi: 在伊斯兰教中,信徒尊称真主为阿拉。
example.pinyin: Zài Yīsīlán jiào zhōng, xìntú zūnchēng zhēnzhǔ wéi Ālā.
example.english: In Islam, believers respectfully refer to God as Allah.
example.fact: During the Hajj pilgrimage, Muslims circle the Kaaba in Mecca seven times in a counterclockwise direction, a ritual called tawaf that is believed to date back to the time of the prophet Abraham.

examples.hanzi: 穆斯林向阿拉祈祷。
examples.pinyin: Mùsīlín xiàng Ālā qídǎo.
examples.english: Muslims pray to Allah.

examples.hanzi: 他在书里读到了关于阿拉的故事。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shū lǐ dú dào le guānyú Ālā de gùshi.
examples.english: He read stories about Allah in a book.

components.note: 手 (hand) — marks hand actions, as in 拿, 打; 摩 is to rub with the hand.
麻 (má) gives the sound: 摩 mó is close, as in 魔 mó and 磨 mó.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: 托 is to hold up with the hand.
乇 (tuō) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 他每天骑摩托车去上班。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān qí mótuōchē qù shàngbān.
example.english: He rides a motorcycle to work every day.
example.fact: The first motorcycle, Gottlieb Daimler's 'Reitwagen,' was built in Germany in 1885. It had a wooden frame, iron-banded wheels, and no suspension, and was designed mainly as a test bed for Daimler's new gasoline engine rather than as practical transportation.

examples.hanzi: 他买了一辆新的摩托。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yí liàng xīn de mótuō.
examples.english: He bought a new motorcycle.

examples.hanzi: 哥哥骑着摩托带我去海边。
examples.pinyin: Gēge qízhe mótuō dài wǒ qù hǎibiān.
examples.english: My older brother took me to the beach on his motorbike.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 招 is to beckon with the hand.
召 (zhào) — near sound — 招 is zhāo; 召 also sounds out 照 zhào and 超 chāo.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 供 is to supply or offer.
共 (gòng) sounds the same except tone; also in 恭 gōng and 洪 hóng.

example.hanzi: 嫌疑人最终向警方招供了。
example.pinyin: Xiányírén zuìzhōng xiàng jǐngfāng zhāogòng le.
example.english: The suspect finally confessed to the police.
example.fact: The Reid Technique, a widely used American interrogation method developed in the 1940s and 1950s, has been criticized by psychologists for sometimes producing false confessions; researchers studying wrongful convictions later overturned by DNA evidence found false confessions were a contributing factor in a notable share of those cases.

examples.hanzi: 在证据面前，他只好招供。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhèngjù miànqián, tā zhǐhǎo zhāogòng.
examples.english: Faced with the evidence, he had no choice but to confess.

examples.hanzi: 小偷被抓后，很快就招供了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu bèi zhuā hòu, hěn kuài jiù zhāogòng le.
examples.english: After the thief was caught, he confessed quickly.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 这支笔只要五十美分。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī bǐ zhǐyào wǔshí Měifēn.
example.english: This pen costs only fifty cents.
example.fact: The United States Mint has reported that producing a single one-cent coin costs more than two cents in metal and manufacturing expenses, meaning the US government loses money every time it makes a penny.

examples.hanzi: 这个糖果一块要二十五美分。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tángguǒ yí kuài yào èrshíwǔ měifēn.
examples.english: This candy costs twenty-five cents a piece.

examples.hanzi: 一美元等于一百美分。
examples.pinyin: Yì měiyuán děngyú yì bǎi měifēn.
examples.english: One dollar equals one hundred cents.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their roles, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 信 trust; 佐 is assisting, a helper, as in 辅佐.
左 (zuǒ) — same sound: 佐 zuǒ. 左 also sounds out 搓 cuō.

example.hanzi: 这个数据可以佐证他的说法。
example.pinyin: Zhège shùjù kěyǐ zuǒzhèng tā de shuōfǎ.
example.english: This data supports what he says.
example.fact: 佐 is a bound form: 佐证 (corroborate), 辅佐 (assist), 佐料 (seasoning) and 佐餐 (to go with a meal).

examples.hanzi: 他的话得到了很多事实佐证。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà dédào le hěn duō shìshí zuǒzhèng.
examples.english: His words have been backed up by a lot of facts.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜里放了一点佐料。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài lǐ fàng le yìdiǎn zuǒliào.
examples.english: A little seasoning was added to this dish.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 皿 is a vessel, as in 盘, 盒; 盗 is coveting what is not yours.
次 (drool) — 次 here originally pictured drooling — wanting something greedily.

example.hanzi: 昨晚有人盗走了他的车。
example.pinyin: Zuówǎn yǒurén dàozǒu le tā de chē.
example.english: Someone stole his car last night.
example.fact: 盗 is bound: 盗版 (pirated), 盗窃 (theft), 强盗 (robber), 海盗 (pirate) and 被盗 (stolen, as in account hacking).

examples.hanzi: 这家店昨晚被盗了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zuówǎn bèi dào le.
examples.english: This shop was robbed last night.

examples.hanzi: 我们要防止盗版软件。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào fángzhǐ dàobǎn ruǎnjiàn.
examples.english: We must prevent pirated software.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 沃 is watering, then fertile, as in 肥沃.
夭 (yāo) — loose sound hint (wò vs yāo).

example.hanzi: 这片土地非常肥沃。
example.pinyin: Zhè piàn tǔdì fēicháng féiwò.
example.english: This land is very fertile.
example.fact: 沃 gives 肥沃 (fertile), 沃土 (rich soil), 沃野千里 and the store name 沃尔玛 (Walmart).

examples.hanzi: 这里的土地肥沃，适合种菜。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de tǔdì féiwò, shìhé zhòng cài.
examples.english: The land here is fertile and good for growing vegetables.

examples.hanzi: 他们在沃土上种了麦子。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài wòtǔ shàng zhòng le màizi.
examples.english: They planted wheat in the rich soil.

components.note: 义 (justice, meaning) also lends its sound to 议 yì discuss, 仪 yí ceremony and 蚁 yǐ ant — a useful clue in many characters.

example.hanzi: 他是一个很讲义气的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn jiǎng yìqì de péngyou.
example.english: He's a friend who is very loyal.
example.fact: 义 is one of the Confucian virtues (仁义礼智信). 义气 is loyalty among friends, 意义 is meaning, 义工 is a volunteer, and 义父 an adoptive father.

examples.hanzi: 这个词的意义是什么？
examples.pinyin: Zhège cí de yìyì shì shénme?
examples.english: What is the meaning of this word?

examples.hanzi: 他做志愿者是出于正义感。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò zhìyuànzhě shì chūyú zhèngyìgǎn.
examples.english: He volunteers out of a sense of justice.

components.note: 月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.
彳 (step) — marks walking and going, as in 行, 往 go toward, 后 behind; 役 is going out to serve or labor.
殳 (shū, weapon in hand) — marks striking or force, as in 设, 投; here it adds the sense of forced labor.

example.hanzi: 他二十岁开始服役。
example.pinyin: Tā èrshí suì kāishǐ fúyì.
example.english: He began his military service at age twenty.
example.fact: Switzerland maintains a militia-based army in which most male citizens complete mandatory service and then keep their government-issued rifle at home between periodic refresher trainings, a long-standing feature of the country's policy of armed neutrality.

examples.hanzi: 他在军队服役了三年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jūnduì fúyì le sān nián.
examples.english: He served in the army for three years.

examples.hanzi: 这艘老船已经服役三十年了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè sōu lǎo chuán yǐjīng fúyì sānshí nián le.
examples.english: This old ship has been in service for thirty years.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
糸 (silk thread; 纟 on the left) — ties and connections, as in 红, 给, 经. 系 is a link or relation.

example.hanzi: 婚前性关系在某些文化中仍被视为禁忌。
example.pinyin: Hūnqián xìngguānxi zài mǒu xiē wénhuà zhōng réng bèi shìwéi jìnjì.
example.english: Premarital sexual relations are still considered taboo in some cultures.
example.fact: Alfred Kinsey's 1948 and 1953 reports on human sexual behavior were among the first large-scale scientific surveys of the topic, drawing on thousands of personal interviews and challenging many assumptions widely held at the time.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章讨论了性关系中的沟通问题。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng tǎolùn le xìngguānxì zhōng de gōutōng wèntí.
examples.english: This article discusses communication problems in sexual relationships.

examples.hanzi: 健康教育课上讲到了安全的性关系。
examples.pinyin: Jiànkāng jiàoyù kè shàng jiǎngdào le ānquán de xìngguānxì.
examples.english: Safe sexual relationships were covered in health class.

meanings: to get off or out of

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 请在下一站下车。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài xià yī zhàn xiàchē.
example.english: Please get off at the next stop.
example.fact: The Brazilian city of Curitiba pioneered the modern 'bus rapid transit' system in the 1970s, using tube-shaped stations where passengers pay their fare before boarding — a design that sped up loading dramatically and has since been copied by cities around the world.

examples.hanzi: 下车的时候请带好行李。
examples.pinyin: Xià chē de shíhou qǐng dài hǎo xíngli.
examples.english: Please take your luggage with you when getting off.

examples.hanzi: 我在下一个路口下车。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài xià yí gè lùkǒu xiàchē.
examples.english: I'll get off at the next intersection.

components.note: 戈 (spear) — two hands (廾) holding a spear: guarding against danger — hence warn, abstain, and 戒指 ring, from the old sense of guarding.
龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.

example.hanzi: 他进入戒毒中心接受治疗。
example.pinyin: Tā jìnrù jièdú zhōngxīn jiēshòu zhìliáo.
example.english: He entered a rehab center for treatment.
example.fact: Methadone maintenance therapy, developed in the 1960s by researchers Vincent Dole and Marie Nyswander, was one of the first medical treatments shown to reduce opioid cravings and withdrawal symptoms without producing the same intense high.

examples.hanzi: 他决心戒毒，重新开始生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéxīn jièdú, chóngxīn kāishǐ shēnghuó.
examples.english: He is determined to quit drugs and start his life over.

examples.hanzi: 戒毒需要家人的支持。
examples.pinyin: Jièdú xūyào jiārén de zhīchí.
examples.english: Quitting drugs requires the support of family.

components.note: 宀 (roof, house) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家 home, 室 room, 安 safe; 宣 was a large hall, where proclamations are made.
禾 (grain) — marks grain and crops, as in 秋, 种, 租; 称 originally meant weighing grain, then naming (称呼).

example.hanzi: 这家公司宣称新产品完全环保。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī xuānchēng xīn chǎnpǐn wánquán huánbǎo.
example.english: This company claims its new product is completely eco-friendly.
example.fact: The term 'greenwashing' was coined in 1986 by environmentalist Jay Westerveld after he noticed hotels asking guests to reuse towels to 'save the environment' while doing comparatively little to reduce their actual environmental impact elsewhere.

examples.hanzi: 他宣称自己没有做过这件事。
examples.pinyin: Tā xuānchēng zìjǐ méiyǒu zuò guo zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: He claimed that he never did this.

examples.hanzi: 网站宣称所有商品都是正品。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngzhàn xuānchēng suǒyǒu shāngpǐn dōu shì zhèngpǐn.
examples.english: The website claims all goods are genuine.

components.note: 首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.
页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.

example.hanzi: 部落首领带领族人迁移到新的土地。
example.pinyin: Bùluò shǒulǐng dàilǐng zúrén qiānyí dào xīn de tǔdì.
example.english: The tribal chief led his people to migrate to new land.
example.fact: Anthropological studies of many hunter-gatherer societies have found that leadership was often situational and non-hereditary, chosen for a specific task like a hunt or a journey, rather than fixed in a permanent chief as once commonly assumed.

examples.hanzi: 这个小组的首领很会安排工作。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎozǔ de shǒulǐng hěn huì ānpái gōngzuò.
examples.english: The leader of this group is good at assigning work.

examples.hanzi: 狼群的首领走在最前面。
examples.pinyin: Lángqún de shǒulǐng zǒu zài zuì qiánmiàn.
examples.english: The leader of the wolf pack walks at the front.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and asking: 说, 谢, 谈; 请 is to ask politely.
青 (qīng) sounds like 请 (tone differs); same part in 清, 情, 晴, 精, 静.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.

example.hanzi: 今天我请客,大家随便点。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ qǐngkè, dàjiā suíbiàn diǎn.
example.english: I'm treating everyone today, order whatever you like.
example.fact: In his influential 1925 study 'The Gift,' anthropologist Marcel Mauss argued that gift-giving and hospitality across widely different cultures follow a similar hidden rule: receiving something, even a shared meal, quietly creates a social obligation to reciprocate later.

examples.hanzi: 今天我生日，晚上我请客。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ shēngrì, wǎnshang wǒ qǐngkè.
examples.english: It's my birthday today, so dinner's on me tonight.

examples.hanzi: 这顿饭谁请客？
examples.pinyin: Zhè dùn fàn shéi qǐngkè?
examples.english: Who is treating us for this meal?

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 按; 抗 is to resist or hold off.
亢 (kàng) gives the sound exactly: 抗 kàng, also in 炕 kàng.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 推, 抱; 拒 is to push back or refuse.
巨 (jù) sounds exactly like 拒; also in 距 jù.

example.hanzi: 他极力抗拒改变旧习惯。
example.pinyin: Tā jílì kàngjù gǎibiàn jiù xíguàn.
example.english: He strongly resists changing his old habits.
example.fact: Habitual behaviors are encoded largely in a brain region called the basal ganglia, which forms efficient neural pathways through repetition — part of why long-standing habits can feel almost automatic and are resistant to conscious change.

examples.hanzi: 孩子很抗拒打针，看见针就哭。
examples.pinyin: Háizi hěn kàngjù dǎzhēn, kànjiàn zhēn jiù kū.
examples.english: The child resists getting shots and cries when he sees a needle.

examples.hanzi: 他对这个安排有些抗拒。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège ānpái yǒuxiē kàngjù.
examples.english: He feels some resistance to this arrangement.

meanings: fig. way out of an embarrassing situation

components.note: 台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.
阝 (hill, from 阜) on the left — marks mounds and steps, as in 院, 队, 附, 陆; 阶 is a stair step.
介 (jiè) hints at the sound: 阶 jiē is close to 界 jiè and 价 jià.

example.hanzi: 老人小心地走下台阶。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén xiǎoxīn de zǒu xià táijiē.
example.english: The old man carefully walked down the steps.
example.fact: The Spanish Steps in Rome, built between 1723 and 1725, consist of 135 steps connecting the Piazza di Spagna at the bottom to the church of Trinità dei Monti at the top, and remain one of the city's most famous meeting spots.

examples.hanzi: 上台阶的时候要小心。
examples.pinyin: Shàng táijiē de shíhou yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: Be careful when you go up the steps.

examples.hanzi: 教堂前面有一段很长的台阶。
examples.pinyin: Jiàotáng qiánmiàn yǒu yí duàn hěn cháng de táijiē.
examples.english: There is a very long flight of steps in front of the church.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 供 is to supply or offer.
共 (gòng) sounds the same except tone; also in 恭 gōng and 洪 hóng.

example.hanzi: 警方记录了目击者的口供。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng jìlù le mùjīzhě de kǒugòng.
example.english: The police recorded the eyewitness's oral statement.
example.fact: Cognitive psychologist Elizabeth Loftus's research beginning in the 1970s showed that eyewitness memory can be distorted by suggestive questioning after the fact, a finding that has since contributed to reforms in how police interview witnesses.

examples.hanzi: 证人的口供前后不一致。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngrén de kǒugòng qiánhòu bù yízhì.
examples.english: The witness's statement was inconsistent.

examples.hanzi: 警察逼他改了口供。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bī tā gǎi le kǒugòng.
examples.english: The police pressured him into changing his statement.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 他在毕业典礼上发表了演说。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bìyè diǎnlǐ shàng fābiǎo le yǎnshuō.
example.english: He delivered a speech at the graduation ceremony.
example.fact: Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech, delivered on August 28, 1963, at the March on Washington, was partly improvised — the famous refrain wasn't part of his prepared remarks and was added spontaneously as he spoke.

examples.hanzi: 市长在广场上发表演说。
examples.pinyin: Shìzhǎng zài guǎngchǎng shàng fābiǎo yǎnshuō.
examples.english: The mayor gave a speech in the square.

examples.hanzi: 她的演说感动了在场的所有人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnshuō gǎndòng le zàichǎng de suǒyǒu rén.
examples.english: Her speech moved everyone present.

components.note: 民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.
矢 (arrow) with a flag 方: a clan or troop gathered under its banner, with arrows at hand.

example.hanzi: 中国是一个多民族国家。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó shì yī gè duō mínzú guójiā.
example.english: China is a multi-ethnic country.
example.fact: Papua New Guinea, with a population of roughly 10 million people, is home to more than 800 distinct languages, making it by far the most linguistically diverse country on Earth relative to its size.

examples.hanzi: 中国有五十六个民族。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒu wǔshíliù gè mínzú.
examples.english: China has fifty-six ethnic groups.

examples.hanzi: 这个民族有自己独特的节日和服饰。
examples.pinyin: Zhège mínzú yǒu zìjǐ dútè de jiérì hé fúshì.
examples.english: This ethnic group has its own distinctive festivals and costumes.

components.note: 西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 这种建筑风格受到西方文化的影响。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jiànzhù fēnggé shòudào Xīfāng wénhuà de yǐngxiǎng.
example.english: This architectural style is influenced by Western culture.
example.fact: For more than 1,500 years starting around the 2nd century BC, the Silk Road network of trade routes carried not just goods like silk and spices but also architectural styles, religions, and technologies back and forth between East and West.

examples.hanzi: 太阳从东方升起，从西方落下。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng cóng dōngfāng shēngqǐ, cóng xīfāng luòxià.
examples.english: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

examples.hanzi: 很多西方游客喜欢来这里旅行。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō xīfāng yóukè xǐhuan lái zhèlǐ lǚxíng.
examples.english: Many Western tourists like traveling here.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 阶, 障; 防 is a dike to guard against floods, then to defend.
方 (fāng) gives the sound: 防 fáng is close, as in 房 fáng and 妨 fáng.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 国防部宣布了新的军事预算。
example.pinyin: Guófángbù xuānbù le xīn de jūnshì yùsuàn.
example.english: The Defense Department announced a new military budget.
example.fact: The Pentagon, headquarters of the US Department of Defense, was built in just sixteen months and completed in 1943. Despite being one of the largest office buildings in the world by floor area, its five-sided ring design means any two points inside are no more than a seven-minute walk apart.

examples.hanzi: 国防部的发言人回答了记者的提问。
examples.pinyin: Guófángbù de fāyánrén huídá le jìzhě de tíwèn.
examples.english: The Ministry of Defense spokesperson answered the reporters' questions.

examples.hanzi: 他曾在国防部工作过很多年。
examples.pinyin: Tā céng zài guófángbù gōngzuò guo hěn duō nián.
examples.english: He worked at the Ministry of Defense for many years.
